$comment: What one run of an agent lane is allowed to spend, enforced by
scripts/agent/budget.mjs. The lanes here already stop on the CLOCK
(agent-dispatch.yml gives the model rounds `timeout-minutes: 12`); this is
the bound on the BILL, which wall-clock cannot see — a prompt that quietly
doubles costs twice as much in the same twelve minutes.
THE UNIT IS TOKENS. They are what the API reports: exact, per call, with no
table to maintain. `prices.models` below is EMPTY on purpose — a price list
is your contract with a provider, it differs per account and it changes
without warning, so the report says 'unpriced' rather than inventing a
figure. Fill it in and every run summary gains a USD column.
A LANE WITH NO ENTRY HERE CANNOT RUN (scripts/agent/budget.mjs fails closed).
That is the point: a new lane is a new bill, and it starts by saying how
large it is allowed to be.
Raising a ceiling is an edit to this file with a 'why'. This file is in
PROTECTED_PREFIXES, so a dispatched agent cannot raise its own ceiling.

dispatch.why: scripts/agent/dispatch.mjs makes exactly two stateless calls — round 1 sends the rubric plus the file inventory, round 2 sends the rubric plus up to MAX_READS (24) files of MAX_READ_BYTES (24 000) each, so round 2 alone is bounded near 150 000 tokens by those constants. maxCalls 2 is therefore exact rather than generous: a third call is a retry loop, not a dispatch.

review.why: scripts/review/agent-review.mjs makes one call carrying the rubric, the commit messages and a diff already capped at KP_REVIEW_DIFF_BUDGET (160 000 characters, about 40 000 tokens). One review is one call; a second means something re-entered it.

prices.$comment: USD per million tokens, by the model id the lane reports. Keys are optional: an unpriced model is reported as unpriced, never as free. `cacheWritePerMTok` defaults to `inputPerMTok` and `cacheReadPerMTok` to 0 when omitted.
